sections.html:
Thomas County borders Florida and centers on Thomasville, which is both the seat and the biggest town. Barwick, Boston, Coolidge, Meigs and Pavo are cities and Ochlocknee is a town. Barwick and Pavo spill over into Brooks County, and Meigs reaches into Mitchell.

Homeowners hold a solid majority here, 63.8% owner-occupancy for 2020-2024, and prices are firm. The 2020 count was 45,798 people, and the mid-2025 estimate is 46,368, growth of 1.3%. The county has 18,684 households, and 21.0% of residents are past their 65th birthday. Builders pulled just 203 permits in 2025, so an older Thomasville bungalow faces little new-construction competition.

Thomasville is the hub of the market, and the Red Hills setting and the Ochlockonee, Suwannee and Aucilla watersheds shape rural parcels in the county's outer areas. For a rural parcel, ask the assessors how acreage is recorded, because that figure feeds the bill.

Public education is split between Thomasville City Schools within the city limits and Thomas County Schools for the rest. A house on one side of that boundary draws a different set of school-minded buyers than one a few blocks over.

sections.h2: Which offices bill and value property
sections.html:
The work is split between two offices. The tax commissioner sends bills and takes payment. The board of tax assessors places a value on each parcel and receives exemption applications.

The tax commissioner is at 225 N. Broad Street, Thomasville 31792, or by mail at P.O. Box 2175, Thomasville 31799. The number is (229) 225-4136. The counter is staffed on weekdays, opening at 8 in the morning and closing at 5, and the office's website posts a holiday closing list.

  • Tax commissioner: bills, payments, delinquent balances, payoff amounts before a tax sale
  • Tax assessor: values, returns, homestead filings, appeals
  • Clerk of Superior Court: recorded deeds and liens
  • Seven city tax departments: Barwick, Boston, Coolidge, Meigs, Ochlocknee, Pavo and Thomasville bill their own residents

County commissioners pick the county rate, the school board picks the school rate, and the state sets its own by law. Someone living in Thomasville may see a city bill on top of the county one, so ask both offices what is owed.

Payment falls due each November 15, and the county takes anything stamped by the post office on or before that day. A bill lost in the mail does not cancel what you owe.

Delinquent totals reset on the sixteenth of every month, so a payoff quote goes stale quickly. Mobile homes pick up penalties each April 2. Skipping a required return carries its own charge: 10% of whatever value went unreported, with interest on top.

  • Regular property tax: November 15
  • Mobile home penalties: added April 2
  • Past-due totals: change on the 16th
  • Unfiled return: 10% of unreported value plus interest

Tax sales happen at the commissioner's discretion, one or two times annually. Call the office for the precise payoff before any sale date, because a figure printed on last year's bill will not match.

The January 1 owner is on the hook for that year's bill. Georgia gives no partial-year refund, which means a deed signed the next day still leaves the whole year with the seller.

Most often the closing attorney asks the commissioner for the balance and deducts it from what the seller nets, or the contract spreads the year across both parties. Request the figure in writing, and ask whether a city bill is also open. Unpaid tax can become a lien filed with the superior court clerk, and a buyer's title company will insist that it be cleared before funds move.

If back tax and deferred repairs pile up on one house, an as-is buyer can absorb both and clear the balance at the closing table. That saves listing prep. It does not erase the debt, because the county is paid either way.

A practical order of work: call the commissioner for the balance, ask the city office if the house sits inside a city, check the clerk's records for any filed lien, and pass every figure to your closing attorney. Bring your parcel number, your last bill and a copy of your deed to any office visit. Doing this before you accept an offer lets you price the house knowing exactly what comes off the top at closing.

Put the challenge on paper and deliver it to the assessors. You get 45 days, starting from the mailing date printed on the assessment notice. The right to appeal comes from O.C.G.A. 48-5-311.

Georgia allows four grounds: taxability, value, uniformity, or a denied exemption. The form must say how you want to proceed, from three choices: an equalization board, a hearing officer, or arbitration. If the assessors and the owner cannot agree, the appeal moves along to the Board of Equalization on its own. Objections to the tax rate are not part of a value appeal.

  • Deadline: 45 days from the notice mailing
  • Where to file: the assessors' office
  • If unresolved: Board of Equalization, then court

Assessed value is set at 40% of market value, measured on the January 1 valuation date. Market value is defined broadly enough to include a short sale, bank sale or auction sale, so a distressed sale of your own home can serve as evidence.

Homestead leads the list, and the form goes to the assessor's office. April 1 is the cutoff, and anything arriving afterward takes effect the next year. Forms are accepted all year long.

Thomas County grants local homestead relief that beats the state version, and the assessor can quote the current amounts. Ask for them directly instead of guessing.

Before you list, confirm the exemption sits on the parcel. A lender and a closing attorney will read the bill, and a missing exemption makes the number look larger than it should. The next owner has to apply for themselves, since a sale partway through the year does not carry your filing forward.

faqs.q: Which phone reaches the Thomas County tax commissioner?
faqs.a: Dial (229) 225-4136. The office sits at 225 N. Broad Street in Thomasville and takes calls on weekdays between 8 in the morning and 5 in the evening. Ask for the assessor's office if your question concerns value or an exemption.

faqs.q: What is the Thomas County property tax deadline?
faqs.a: November 15 each year, with mail postmarked by that day accepted. Overdue amounts change on the 16th of every month, and mobile home penalties begin April 2.

faqs.q: Will selling erase this year's tax in Thomas County?
faqs.a: No. Georgia returns nothing for a partial year, so the January 1 owner carries that bill. At closing the attorney typically settles it out of the seller's proceeds, or the contract shares it.

faqs.q: How many days does an assessment appeal allow in Thomas County?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the date the notice went out in the mail. Write to the assessors, and mark your preferred hearing path on the form.

faqs.q: Does Thomasville bill its own tax separately?
faqs.a: Yes. Barwick, Boston, Coolidge, Meigs, Ochlocknee, Pavo and Thomasville each collect their own city taxes. Contact that city's tax department for the city portion.
